title: Find the fault
summary: Diagnose a beam that sticks on while the line is sorting: compare its signal with how long a box can really break it, and stop the line before it misroutes a box.
scope: Tests give deterministic native POSIX host evidence on a simulated plant scene; they are not physical, hardware, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Diagnose a stuck sensor from a fact the program can read, not from the sensor itself.
Choose a safe reaction: stop what brings new boxes and let the boxes already moving arrive.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/HeightSortChain.st the sorter of lesson 16.4 works while the sensors tell the truth. Add a diagnosis: a box breaks BeamHigh for about a second, so a TON of three seconds on High marks the beam as stuck. Latch a Fault, then stop the infeed and the chain module, keep the blade holding and put Busy out.
stages.checkpoint: After the fault the infeed is off, Busy and Done are off, the blade still holds, and no box has gone to the wrong bin.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario triggers the fault action stuckOn on BeamHigh at {{t:21000}} ms, while boxes keep arriving every five seconds. Before running, say which boxes the stuck beam makes look different, and which bin a program without a diagnosis sends them to.
stages.checkpoint: Every box that is not tall breaks BeamLow and the stuck BeamHigh, so it looks tall and goes left to BinTall; the diagnosis must stop the line before that.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter sorts correctly but trusts BeamHigh for ever; when the beam sticks on, boxes that are not tall are sent to BinTall, so latch a fault when High stays on for three seconds and stop the line.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: In Tests, choose the saved zplc.json and run only the fault-actions scenario; watch the 3D view while it runs.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named fault-actions and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Trigger the fault yourself in the 3D view (BeamHigh, stuckOn) and watch High in the trace: it stays TRUE while boxes come and go. About three seconds later Fault latches, the infeed stops and Busy goes out.
stages.checkpoint: High stays TRUE for far longer than any box needs to pass, and the stop follows the fault, not a box.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The grade sees what the plant did: no misrouted box in any bin, the infeed off and the blade holding at the end. It does not see your Fault variable or the three seconds you chose; a limit that is too short stops the line at the first tall box and fails.
stages.checkpoint: This rule catches a beam stuck on. A beam stuck off, or a jam of the chain module, needs another rule; the grade does not establish sensor behaviour on real hardware, HIL, or certification.

hints.text: A normal box breaks BeamHigh for about a second. Use Stuck(IN := High, PT := T#3000ms), latch Fault := TRUE when Stuck.Q is TRUE and never clear it.

Stop what brings new boxes: RunIn and RunChain get AND NOT Fault, Stand gets AND NOT Fault so that no box is routed on a reading you do not trust, and Busy goes out. Leave the three outfeed belts running so that a box already on its way arrives.

faultCases: The starter sorts correctly but trusts BeamHigh for ever; when the beam sticks on, boxes that are not tall are sent to BinTall, so latch a fault when High stays on for three seconds and stop the line.
